changelog: Insert a new core principle allowing safe splits immediately after sentence-introductory function words when the remainder is semantically self-contained — addresses the primary finding about excessive reluctance to split short left pieces.
Replace example E1 with a measured labeled example en_us_845 (short-latency case that rewards an early cut) so the model learns the ranking from data.

Insert a core principle permitting safe cuts immediately after a main verb when the remainder is a short, self-contained predicate or closed complement — addresses the primary finding that a blanket verb–cut prohibition harms very short, low-latency segments.

Insert a core principle forbidding cuts between numerals/quantifiers and their units or quantified nouns — directly addresses the primary finding that splitting numerals from their units causes severe cohesion loss.

Insert a narrow, surface-check core principle that permits a cut immediately after a single sentence‑initial function word under concrete token conditions; addresses the primary finding that the prompt was too reluctant to split off short sentence-introductory function words and supplies a recognisable, checkable rule.

Insert a narrow surface rule permitting cuts after a verb when the remainder is a short, closed prepositional span — lets safe short verb+PP separations improve low-latency segmentation without retuning broad verb-cut scope.

Insert a narrow surface rule forbidding cuts between a numeral/quantifier and its immediately following unit word or quantified noun — a concrete, source-form check to protect numeral+unit spans (obeys the 'narrow_rule' constraint).
Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_292 to teach the model that splitting immediately after an initial determiner ('The') can be optimal in short-latency cases.
Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_884 to show that sentence‑introductory prepositional/adverbial leads ('In') are often safe early cuts.
Replace E3 with labeled example en_us_46 to supply a measured case where an early temporal/location lead ('On') should be split for better low-latency performance.
Replace E4 with labeled example en_us_482 to provide a contrasted case where an early subject/head ('Mysticism') is best delivered early and an initial predicate cut is rewarded.

Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_301 to teach that sentence‑initial participial/adverbial leads can often be emitted early when the remainder is self‑contained (addresses the critique that the prompt was too reluctant to split off short initial function words).

Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_340 to supply a measured case showing a safe short predicate/complement split after a verb (directly addresses the primary finding that a blanket ban on cuts after main verbs is too broad).

Replace E3 with labeled example en_us_924 to add a measured example where a closed complement/short prepositional span following a verb is safe to cut (reinforces allowing safe verb‑adjacent splits without retuning broad rules).
Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_1116 to teach the model to keep numerals/quantifiers attached to their unit or quantified noun (addresses the primary finding about numeral+unit cohesion loss).
Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_860 to show a measured case where cutting between '10' and 'years' hurts fidelity, reinforcing protection of numeral+unit spans.
Replace E3 with labeled example en_us_1024 to provide another measured short-latency case ('two summer Olympics') that rewards keeping numerals with their units/nouns.

Insert a concise core principle allowing cuts after initial sentence-introductory function words when the remainder is semantically self-contained — addresses the primary finding that the prompt was too reluctant to split very short left pieces that help low-latency performance.

Insert a narrow surface rule allowing safe cuts after a main verb when the remainder is very short and contains no clause-openers, negation, or pronouns — addresses the primary finding that a blanket verb-cut prohibition harmed very short, low-latency segments.
Insert a concise core principle forbidding cuts between a numeral/quantifier and its immediately following unit or quantified noun — to protect numeral+unit spans as the primary finding requires.
